dedupe_keys.name: wastewater treatment plants within 2 km of the us coastline sea level rise exposure dataset

description: This dataset locates the wastewater treatment plants that lie within 2 km of the US coastline, taken from the US Environmental Protection Agency's Facility Registry Service and checked against imagery to correct their positions, and adds an interpolated depth-to-groundwater surface for the San Francisco Bay Area. It supports a study of how sea level rise, including rising groundwater, threatens coastal wastewater systems. Researchers at UC Berkeley and Argonne National Laboratory published it on Dryad in March 2018 as a free download under CC0. Coverage is national for coastal plants, with groundwater only for the Bay Area. Caveats: plant attributes such as capacity are not described on the record, the file formats were not listed, and the locations date from about 2017. Simulation uses: exposure of coastal treatment plants to sea level rise and storm surge for climate adaptation and resilience planning. Related records: the Clean Watersheds Needs Survey (data-epa-clean-watersheds-needs-survey-2022) and HydroWASTE (data-hydrowaste).
